headline: USCG Warns: Verify Air Draft Before Bridges
subheadline: Marine Safety Alert 17-26 after a bridge strike
insight: A ship hit a bridge after old plans left out a tiltable MF/HF antenna, so the pilot got an understated air draft. USCG: verify configuration before every transit.

sources.title: USCG Warns Shipowners to Verify Air Draft, Avoid Bridge Strike
USCG issues safety alert on vessel air draft calculations following bridge contact

factCheck.notes: Corroborated by two independent trade reports of the USCG alert: Marine Safety Alert 17-26 issued 10 Nov 2026, developed by Sector Los Angeles-Long Beach and distributed by the Office of Investigations and Casualty Analysis (MarineLink). Both report the same finding: a deep-draft vessel struck a bridge although voyage planning showed sufficient clearance; outdated plans omitted an installed MF/HF tiltable antenna, so the pilot was given an understated air draft. Vessel name, bridge and incident date not published, so none are stated. The USCG safety-alert index page was not yet updated when checked. Alert is 4 days old and is presented as a 10 Nov alert, not as new today.

image.credit: U.S. Navy (Bureau of Ships) / Wikimedia Commons

meta.description: The U.S. Coast Guard issued Marine Safety Alert 17-26 on 10 November 2026 after a deep-draft vessel struck a bridge even though its voyage-planning calculations showed enough vertical clearance. Investigators found the reported air draft came from outdated plans that did not show an installed MF/HF tiltable antenna, so the pilot was given an understated air draft and the antenna was not lowered. The USCG recommends building air-draft verification into the safety management system, keeping current vessel-specific drawings, removing superseded plans, and positively confirming that antennas and other movable equipment are lowered before overhead-clearance transits.
meta.question: When did your ship last re-measure its air draft against the current drawings, including every antenna and mast?
meta.altText: Representative U.S. Navy archive photo of a cargo ship passing under a bridge, with HeyMariner safety card text on USCG Marine Safety Alert 17-26 about verifying air draft before bridge transits.
